speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Prime Minister as "Buy Now Pay Later" (BNPL) schemes have rapidly gained traction in the past year (a) what is the total value of BNPL transactions in Singapore in 2021; (b) whether there are plans for BNPL companies and schemes to be regulated; and (c) whether BNPL schemes have disproportionately affected younger consumers in being over-leveraged.

speaker: The Minister of State (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Some common features of BNPL schemes limit the extent of debt accumulation by consumers.

speaker: The Minister of State (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For example, BNPL providers typically suspend users from making further BNPL purchases once a payment is overdue.

speaker: The Minister of State (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: BNPL schemes also do not charge compounding interest on the outstanding amount and cap the amount of late fees levied.

speaker: The Minister of State (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The risk of rapid debt accumulation by consumers through BNPL schemes is, hence, not large.

speaker: The Minister of State (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: All BNPL providers in Singapore have also set a minimum account opening age requirement of at least 18.

speaker: The Minister of State (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We are studying the experience of other countries where BNPL schemes have taken off more strongly.

speaker: The Minister of State (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS will continue to guide the progress of the BNPL Working Group and monitor developments in this space.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The consumer can purchase across multiple shopping sites and use multiple BNPL facilities provided by different providers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Should there not be a limit to how much a person can utilise such facilities?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: BNPL also has the propensity to encourage spending beyond one's means, especially because BNPL payments are charged to a buyer's credit card so there is double leverage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can MAS consider making credit worthiness checks on BNPL, similar to what it has been doing for credit cards?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS agrees with the risks highlighted by the Member.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As I had mentioned earlier in my response, the BNPL's code of conduct will seek to enshrine unique features of BNPLs which exist today to limit the extent of debt accumulation by users.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS is monitoring the progress of the BNPL code and will continue to guide its development, especially in areas where MAS has baseline expectations that need to be met within the code.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: At this point of time, I want to quickly just share on what consumers may do while we are still working with the SFA on this code.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As with undertaking any financing of any form, consumers should first consider and prioritise their needs over wants when deciding to make a purchase.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: BNPL schemes and instalment plans should not be used as a way to buy items that are more expensive than what consumers can afford and do not need.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: By over-stretching finances this way, consumers compromise on their financial goals.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Consumers should read and understand the terms of any financing schemes, including BNPL schemes, which are fast gaining popularity, before signing up for any of these schemes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In particular, they should be aware of any fees and charges, such as late fees, which are imposed on missed or partial payments.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Consumers need to be sure they are able to make payments fully and promptly and factor in whether they can bear the consequences of failing to do so.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The Consumers Association of Singapore is concerned with the risk posed by the BNPL scheme, especially when the consumer is unable to service the payment instalments.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, while I can understand that the Government needs time to study the evolving BNPL landscape and consider its regulatory approach, I would like to ask will MAS consider including advertising curbs in the proposed code that it is studying right now, similar to that which is imposed on cryptocurrency.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is so as to prevent BNPL schemes from preying on impressionable youths.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think it is a very important point.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And I also encourage the Member and CASE also to work together with the Singapore FinTech Association and the Working Group to explore some of the suggestions that he has made.
